correctness.rationale: Point-subspace incidence is a symmetric 2-design with explicit diagonal and off-diagonal Gram entries. Centering yields T*T=c(I-J/v), c=BR(v-R)/(v(v-1))>0, so E1=TT*/c has rank v-1 and exactly the displayed kernel. For n>=2k and all q>=2, [k]_q^2/[n]_q<1, proving negative kernel entries occur exactly on disjoint subspaces, with none on the diagonal. The #disjoint spaces is q^(k^2) Gaussian(n-k,k) by graph-of-linear-map counting. Since every row has zero sum, its absolute row sum is exactly twice the negative mass. Symmetry gives l1 norm; diagonal (v-1)/B gives complement norm. Gaussian-product rewriting proves the fixed-excess Euler limit. Exact-fraction checks cover 500 q-binomial cases and 15 independent explicit-space cases but do not replace the proof.

originality.rationale: Primary comparisons reconstruct the claim at the level of implications. General finite-homogeneous Fourier decomposition (Scarabotti–Tolli), full Grassmann eigenbases (Srinivasan), and first-degree point indicators/Boolean classification (Filmus–Ihringer) identify the spectral object but do not supply its absolute-value row mass, exact endpoint operator norm, complementary norm, or balanced q-Euler-product coefficient. The new sign threshold for the centered incidence kernel, the disjoint-subspace enumeration in the absolute row sum, and its balanced limit supply the missing quantitative statement. Quantitative endpoint claims in adjacent Johnson and Walsh harmonic settings were also compared for implication coverage. A hidden equivalent in older q-Hahn association-scheme literature is a residual originality risk; unsuccessful searches alone do not establish novelty.
residual_risks: An earlier exact value may be implicit in association-scheme tables for primitive idempotents after summing q-Hahn polynomial absolute values; the reviewed sources did not state that norm.
The accessible published literature is not a guarantee against equivalent results in inaccessible or unindexed sources.

value.rationale: The rank-(v-1) eigenspace is the canonical first nonconstant harmonic stratum of every finite q-Grassmannian; its sharp endpoint amplification is a natural quantitative norm not determined by the existence of an eigenbasis. The formula gives a complete all-prime-power/all-dimension evaluation and the balanced limit exhibits a genuine codimension-sensitive q-Euler-product coefficient. The result is a finite-geometry analogue with qualitatively different growth from the existing degree-two Johnson/Walsh endpoint constants, rather than an arbitrary finite table or a cosmetic parameter change. The elementary incidence identities alone do not state the absolute operator-norm invariant; the sign classification and asymptotic make the exact endpoint statement useful.
